verdict.root_cause: An automated platform change at 05:53:46 rewrote cartservice's Redis backing-store address to a target on port 6380 (tr_81bd1cfe0ec8). cartservice cannot establish a connection to redis-cart at that endpoint; the connect attempt times out after ~15-40s and throws an unhandled exception out of RedisCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected -> InitializeAsync -> Program.Main, so the process crash-loops at startup and never reaches a serving state (tr_53476e44e67f). With cartservice unavailable, checkoutservice's first downstream step — the outbound CartService/GetCart call inside prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart — fails immediately, and that error propagates up through PlaceOrder to the frontend, which is why checkoutservice, frontend and loadgenerator all alerted at 05:56:30 (tr_86d0e8624dca). checkoutservice itself is blameless: no changes on it (tr_bd5c71d3706d), it keeps accepting orders and logs no errors of its own, but no PlaceOrder after ~05:55 ever reaches the payment/email/message-write steps (tr_af6d4aa36488), and its error ratio is elevated but partial, consistent with intermittent success while cart replicas cycle (tr_5cc20e61b736).
verdict.reasoning: Three independent layers converge on one story. Traces establish the causal direction and the failing edge: the deepest error-bearing span in every sampled failing checkout is checkoutservice's outbound GetCart, the enclosing prepare span carries no independent error, and frontend spans error only after their child does — so origin is at or below cartservice, not in checkout logic or the frontend (tr_86d0e8624dca). checkout's own logs corroborate the shape without naming a culprit: orders keep arriving, no error severity is emitted, and the completion lines for payment/email/message-write vanish after ~05:55, i.e. requests die at the first downstream step (tr_af6d4aa36488). cartservice logs supply the mechanism: every error in the window is a Redis connect failure to port 6380 thrown unhandled from Program.Main, meaning the process never serves, and normal cart operations were healthy earlier at ~05:46 (tr_53476e44e67f). The change log supplies the trigger and the timing: a single automated env-var edit at 05:53:46 setting exactly that Redis address, under three minutes before onset, with no deploy or flag change competing for the explanation (tr_81bd1cfe0ec8). Latency mechanisms are excluded — root spans complete in 1-3ms and erroring leaves sub-millisecond, so this is fast-fail, not saturation or deadline exhaustion (tr_86d0e8624dca) — which also rules out resource_exhaustion at the checkout tier. cartservice's absent calls_total series is a telemetry gap, not a signal, and is consistent with a process that never reaches serving state, but it was not usable as corroboration (tr_887fa4128382). Because the fault is an injected/incorrect configuration value rather than code, reverting the env var to the working Redis endpoint (and letting the crash-looping pods restart into it) is the corrective action; a rollback of any image would not touch the offending value.
open_questions: No prior value was recorded for the Redis address (tr_81bd1cfe0ec8), so it is unsettled whether 6380 is a wrong port versus a first-time injection of a setting that previously came from a default — this changes what 'revert' means in practice.

It is not confirmed from evidence here whether any Redis instance actually listens on 6380, or whether the correct endpoint is 6379; the connect timeout duration hints at an unreachable host/port rather than a refusal, but that was not directly verified.
Why platform-automation made the change is entirely unexamined — a reconciliation loop, template change, or pipeline could re-apply the bad value immediately after a revert.

The ~4-minute gap between the config edit at 05:53:46 and the first cartservice Redis errors at ~05:57:51 (tr_53476e44e67f) is unexplained; it is plausibly rollout/pod-cycling lag but no pod or restart evidence was gathered to confirm it, and alerting fired at 05:56:30, before the first observed cart error line.

cartservice has no usable request/error metrics under the queried labels (tr_887fa4128382); no memory, restart-count, or cache-connection metrics were retrieved at all, so replica-level behaviour and any concurrent resource pressure are unverified.

checkoutservice's error ratio is partial rather than total (tr_5cc20e61b736) while every sampled trace failed identically (tr_86d0e8624dca); the successful fraction was never characterised — possibly stale-cache or non-checkout call paths, possibly sampling bias.

Triage flagged 4 unmeasured edges; accountingservice, currencyservice and paymentservice are argued out because checkout aborts before reaching them (tr_86d0e8624dca), but that argument covers only these failing checkout traces and does not prove those services are healthy or uninvolved in the broader 12-service blast radius.
The other 9 services in the blast radius were never dispatched on; whether their alerts are all downstream of cart or include an independent problem is unestablished.
